note: Faithful rendering of Avalokitavrata's gloss on 'when debated by means of emptiness', with the MMK 1.1 verse correctly set as verse; only inline glosses clutter it.
Grammatically careful rendering of the ablative-case and bahuvrihi discussion; argument structure preserved.

errors.english: for the purpose of reversing conceptual thought (kalpana) that perceives a contradictory nature
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'non-mistaken' excludes cognition that is free from conceptual thought yet grasps a contradictory nature (non-conceptual error); dropping 'free from' (dang bral ba) inverts the point, since conceptual cognition is excluded by a different qualifier.

fix.find: for the purpose of reversing conceptual thought (kalpana) that perceives a contradictory nature
fix.replace: for the purpose of excluding cognition that is free from conceptual thought (kalpana) yet perceives a contradictory nature

errors.why: dbyibs is shape (saṃsthāna), not ākāra, which is rnam pa (aspect).

errors.english: Is this not done so that valid cognition (pramana) reliable knowledge or a valid means of knowing does not become mistaken?
errors.why: The objection is that the qualifier is stated so that one does not mistake such a cognition for a pramāṇa, not so that pramāṇa does not become mistaken.

note: Readable, but the key sentence on what 'non-mistaken' (abhrānta) excludes is inverted, and a term is mis-equated.

errors.english: The opponent says: "From the familiarity of others," and so forth.
errors.why: gzhan gyi marks the cited words as the opponent's ('the other's [statement]: "from familiarity"'), as in the parallel gzhan gyi ste just above; it is not familiarity belonging to others.

errors.english: Others, thinking it is impossible to deny the experienced object, show the sequence
errors.why: The author shows the sequence of engagement lest others think the experienced object cannot be shown/denied; 'others' are not the ones showing it.

note: The pramāṇa debate on attainment and familiarity is followed well; two attributions of who speaks or acts are off.
Faithful rendering of the argument that a permanent cause cannot acquire a new productive nature and that destruction needs no cause.
Accurate on the god/human continuum argument and the opponent's dilemma about the reason; inline name glosses are distracting but harmless.

span_why: The opening sentence (bed with lapis legs, golden canopy, beings with golden lotuses in hand) translates the previous side's last line.

errors.english: Surrounded on all sides by the masters of the (Yakshas) nature spirits or guardians of wealth, invisible gods also dwelled in the sky.
errors.why: The yakṣa lords stood surrounding the newborn on all sides; it is not the invisible gods who are surrounded by them.

note: A fluent verse paraphrase of the nativity wonders, faithful in substance, though it pulls in the previous side's last line.

errors.english: "sublimating evidence" (gnod pa can gyi tshad ma)
errors.why: gnod pa can gyi tshad ma is bādhakapramāṇa, the invalidating (refuting) valid cognition, not 'sublimating evidence'.

fix.find: "sublimating evidence" (gnod pa can gyi tshad ma)
fix.replace: "invalidating valid cognition" (gnod pa can gyi tshad ma, bādhakapramāṇa)

note: Sound rendering of the momentariness argument and the opponent's non-pervasion doubt; one technical term is badly mis-rendered.
Careful rendering of the latrine-etiquette root lines and their glosses; the interleaving of root and commentary is preserved.

errors.english: close relatives and those who perform religious duties
errors.why: rim gro byas pa here means those who have rendered one service or honour (benefactors/attendants), not people performing religious duties.

note: Faithful account of the hell punishments for sexual misconduct; one category in the closing list is misread.
